## Proof

The matrix $M$ is the bi-infinite Toeplitz operator on $\ell(\mathbb{Z})$ with symbol determined by diagonal entry $25$ and first off-diagonal entries $-6$ (the second off-diagonal entries are $0$, so $M$ is effectively tridiagonal).

For $y = (y_i)_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} \in \ell(\mathbb{Z})$,

$$
\langle My, y\rangle = \sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} 25\,y_i^2 - 6\,y_i\,y_{i+1} - 6\,y_{i-1}\,y_i = \sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} 25\,y_i^2 - 12\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} y_i\,y_{i+1}.
$$

**Key inequality.** By the AM–GM inequality (equivalently $(y_i - y_{i+1})^2 \ge 0$),

$$
2\,y_i\,y_{i+1} \le y_i^2 + y_{i+1}^2,
$$

hence

$$
-12\,y_i\,y_{i+1} \ge -6\bigl(y_i^2 + y_{i+1}^2\bigr).
$$

Summing over all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ (all series converge absolutely since $y\in\ell(\mathbb{Z})$):

$$
-12\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} y_i\,y_{i+1} \ge -6\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}\bigl(y_i^2 + y_{i+1}^2\bigr) = -12\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} y_i^2,
$$

where the last equality uses the translation invariance of the index set $\mathbb{Z}$ (shifting $i+1\mapsto i$).

Therefore

$$
\langle My, y\rangle \ge 25\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} y_i^2 - 12\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} y_i^2 = 13\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} y_i^2 = 13\,\|y\|^2.
$$

**Sharpness.** The bound $13$ is attained in the limit. Consider the finite section of size $N$ and the test vector $y^{(N)}$ with $y_i = \sin\!\bigl(\tfrac{\pi i}{N+1}\bigr)$ for $i=1,\dots,N$. The Rayleigh quotient of the tridiagonal Toeplitz matrix with diagonal $25$ and off-diagonal $-6$ on this eigenvector is

$$
25 + 2(-6)\cos\!\frac{\pi}{N+1} = 25 - 12\cos\!\frac{\pi}{N+1} \xrightarrow{N\to\infty} 25 - 12 = 13.
$$

Equivalently, the spectrum of the bi-infinite Toeplitz operator with symbol $m(\theta) = 25 - 12\cos\theta$ is $[13, 37]$, so the infimum of $\langle My,y\rangle/\|y\|^2$ is exactly $13$.

$$
\boxed{\langle My, y\rangle \ge 13\,\|y\|^2.}
$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
